lines.text: For five thousand years it has watched the sands — the Sphinx, silent, eternal, guarding the kingdom of the Pharaohs. Egypt, the oldest crown in the game, does not bow.
But from the far side of the world come the Socceroos — fearless, relentless, riding under the Southern Cross. Tonight, the Sphinx meets the stars.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode ninety. Egypt, versus Australia. A knockout. Win, or the dream dies right here.
Egypt arrive as the kings of Africa — seven-time champions of their continent, led by a living legend. Australia arrive as the Socceroos — no stars, no fear, all heart.
Egypt — the Pharaohs. Ancient, proud, and blessed with the greatest of them all.

Mohamed Salah is the pharaoh himself, the captain who bends whole nights to his will. Omar Marmoush is the young fire beside him, fast and fearless. And Mahmoud Trezeguet flies down the flank like a desert wind.
Mohamed Elneny holds the middle with quiet iron. And at the back, the wall of Egypt stands firm, calm as ancient stone.
Australia — the Socceroos. Under the Southern Cross, a team that never, ever stops running.
Aaron Mooy is the maestro, threading the game together. Jackson Irvine, the captain, is the engine that never dies. And Craig Goodwin burns down the left with a cannon in his boot.
Mitchell Duke leads the line with a warrior's heart. And Riley McGree brings the spark, young and hungry.
So here is the riddle. Does the Sphinx guard the crown, as it always has? Or do the Socceroos steal a night written in the stars?
And stay with me — because this one turns, late, on the touch of a pharaoh.
Here is how we see it. Australia come out flying, all pressure and running, and the ancient kingdom is rocked.
The Socceroos strike first. The whole of Egypt holds its breath.
And it lands. Australia bundle it home, and the underdogs lead. The Southern Cross burns bright.
But the Sphinx does not fall. Egypt steady, the ball finds Salah, and the temple wakes.
And Mohamed Salah levels it — one-one. The pharaoh has spoken.
And then, late, the dagger. Omar Marmoush strikes, and Egypt lead. Two — one. The crown holds.
Two — one. Australia were magnificent, and fearless, and so nearly there — but the Sphinx would not be moved.
Our prediction — Egypt two, Australia one. Marmoush, late. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
And Australia leave with their heads high — the Socceroos who ran the kings of Africa to the very last breath.
Egypt march on. The Sphinx, reminding the world that some crowns are older than time itself.
So you tell me — the Sphinx, or the stars? Comment EGYPT for the Pharaohs — comment AUSTRALIA for the Socceroos.
It has knelt at the edge of the desert since before history began — a lion's body, a king's face, the silent guardian of a thousand pharaohs. Legend ninety — the Sphinx.
The players write the night. But the Sphinx carries one truth — kingdoms rise and fall, yet some things simply endure. You only have to outlast the storm.
Here is how. Go to worldcup twenty-six dot world and create your free account — ten seconds, and the Sphinx, Legend ninety, unlocks instantly.
Then pick three of the forty-eight nations, and every goal they score, scores for you. Free to play, just for fun. No prizes — only glory.
So sign up tonight, claim your Legend, and send this to someone who never stops running. Hit like, subscribe — and I'll see you when the next legend rises.
